propositions: Fixture setup is 47% of tests/interfaces wall-clock because rebar_repo spawns 58 git processes per test (306ms each); building a session-scoped template once per xdist worker and copying it reduces this to 22.3ms (13.7x speedup).

Template copies require four independent fix-ups: rewrite both linked-worktree pointers (.git and gitdir) to resolve to the copy's path, set REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR per test to avoid snapshot store collisions, re-randomize .env-id and .signing-key unconditionally after each copy, and reset the module-global _pending_cache.

Bare git worktree repair silently fails to fix copies and corrupts the template when run against the SOURCE; only explicit pointer rewriting guarantees correctness, which the tier-wide autouse guard enforces by validating git worktree list --porcelain paths fall inside REBAR_ROOT.

The session-scoped template fixture must build inside its own MonkeyPatch context that pins REBAR_ROOT, clears XDG_CONFIG_HOME and environment config keys, and calls reset_config_cache on entry/exit to prevent test autouse environment from contaminating the template.

Deliberate coverage of the build-from-scratch path is preserved in test_init_idempotent_scratch.py and test_e4_init.py; the template scheme removes only incidental coverage from 589 function-scoped init_repo calls.

Durable sentinel tests in test_rebar_repo_isolation.py verify the guard rejects half-fixed and bare-repaired copies, confirm no template path leaks into copies, prove writes in one copy do not advance other stores' refs, and enforce that the virgin template contains no tickets and no .rebar/.
